title: MicroRNA Sequencing Protocol for Porcine Skeletal Muscle
author: Dongting He
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.idsca6e
materials: using NCBI Local BLAST, including three steps: (

steps.title: Sample Collection and Storage
steps.instruction: Isolate longissimus dorsi (LD) muscle tissues from pigs, immediately freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at -80℃ until RNA isolation.

steps.title: Total RNA Isolation and Quality Control
steps.instruction: Isolate total RNA from muscle samples and verify quality.

substeps.instruction: Isolate total RNA using the mirVana TM miRNA isolation kit (Ambion, Austin, USA).
Measure total RNA quality and purity using a Bioanalyzer 2100 and RNA 6000 Nano LabChip Kit (Agilent, CA, USA), ensuring RIN > 7.0.

steps.title: Small RNA Library Construction
steps.instruction: Prepare small RNA libraries using approximately 1 μg of total RNA per sample following the TruSeq Small RNA Sample Prep Kits (Illumina, San Diego, USA) protocol.

substeps.instruction: Excise 10~40 nt RNA fragments and purify from a polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE).
Ligate fragments with 5’ and 3’ adaptors using T4 RNA ligase.
Reverse transcribe and amplify the modified small RNA via RT-PCR.
Purify amplified cDNA constructs from agarose gel.
Quantify enriched cDNA using a Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent, CA, USA).
Sequence the library in a HiSeq 2500 sequencing system (Illumina, San Diego, USA) at LC-BIO (Hangzhou, China).

steps.title: Raw Read Filtering and Processing
steps.instruction: Process raw sequencing reads to isolate high-quality miRNA reads.

substeps.instruction: Filter raw reads using the Illumina pipeline filter (Solexa 0.3).
Use the ACGT101-miR program (LC Science, Houston, Texas, USA) to remove sequencing adapters, junk reads, and fragments < 26 nt.
Search remaining 18~26 nt reads against Rfam, NCBI, and Repbase databases to remove non-miRNAs (rRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, mRNA, and repeats) to obtain 'mappable reads'.

steps.title: miRNA Mapping and Identification
steps.instruction: Map mappable reads to the pig genome (Sscrofa 10.2) using NCBI Local BLAST to identify known, conserved, and candidate miRNAs.

substeps.instruction: Align mappable reads to porcine pre-miRNAs/miRNAs, then to pre-miRNAs/miRNAs from 25 other mammals in miRBase 21.0.
Search mapped pre-miRNAs/miRNAs against the pig genome to determine genomic locations and annotations in Ensemble (Sscrofa 10.2).
Blast unmapped sequences against pig genomes and predict hairpin RNA structures from the flank 80 nt sequences using RNAfold software.
Categorize identified miRNAs as porcine known (ssc-miR-), porcine conserved (PC-), or porcine candidate/novel (PN-).
Assemble identified miRNAs into porcine unique miRNAs and normalize expression by total mappable reads.

steps.title: Differential Expression Analysis
steps.instruction: Identify differentially expressed (DE) miRNAs between treatment groups.

substeps.instruction: Compare normalized miRNA reads (> 1000 read counts in either treatment 1 or 2) using a Student t-test with a significance threshold of 0.05.
Select the top 50 most abundant DE miRNAs based on total read counts for further analysis.

steps.title: Target Prediction and Functional Annotation
steps.instruction: Predict target genes for the most abundant and DE miRNAs and perform pathway analysis.

substeps.instruction: Identify miRNA binding sites using TargetScan 6.2 and miRanda (using human miRNAs as porcine genes were unavailable in those versions).
Combine data from both algorithms and calculate overlaps.
Annotate Gene Ontology (GO) terms and KEGG Pathways of targets using DAVID bioinformatics resources (http://david.abcc.ncifcrf.gov/).
Submit small RNA sequence data and processed files to NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO).

steps.title: miRNA Quantification and Validation
steps.instruction: Quantify miRNA levels and validate sequencing results using qPCR.

substeps.instruction: Perform S-poly(T) miRNA qPCR-assay using the reagent kit (Geneups, China).
Use SnoRNA-202 (mouse internal reference) as the internal control for normalization.
Analyze real-time PCR data using the 2^-ΔΔCt method, expressing miRNA as the fold of the mean of treatment 1 group.
Analyze DE miRNAs among six samples (two treatments, three replicates each) using two-way ANOVA with breeds and time points as factors.
Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient (r) and significance value (P) using SPSS software, defining statistical significance as P < 0.05.
